title: Afterglow Watch — Late Shift Bulletpad (draft)
content:
TL;DR: quick checks + ephemeral fixes for late shift. Use this as a scratchpad — copy important bits into the official runbook if they actually work.

Context / mental model:
- Night traffic is usually lower but noisier: batch jobs run at ~02:00 UTC and sometimes saturate inference queues.
- Common problems: model mount flaps, autoscaler thrash, or one-off GPU OOMs after weird input.
- This doc is my late-shift cheat list + things I wish I'd known at 03:47.

Quick startup checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Slack -> #oncall-night: ping 'ani' if anything is already flagged.
2) Open Console -> Routes -> `prod/*` -> look for alerts with >3m spikes.
3) Grafana dashboards to glance: p50/p95 latency, GPU mem usage (per-pod), request queue length.
4) kubectl get pods -n inference | grep CrashLoop or OOMKilled
5) Check capacity: `kubectl top nodes` + compare GPU alloc fraction against baseline (usually < 0.7).

Key quick commands (copy/paste):
- List recent crashloops (last 1 hour):
  kubectl get pods -n inference -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.containerStatuses[].restartCount>0) | {name:.metadata.name, restarts:.status.containerStatuses[].restartCount}'
- Restart a router pod (safe during low traffic):
  kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-router -n inference
- Check node GPU memory pressure (NVIDIA):
  kubectl exec -it <pod> -n inference -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv

Common incident patterns + first-pass fixes:
A) High p95 latency across routes, no obvious CPU/GPU saturation:
- Check cache hit rate on prefix cache (Console -> Optimize -> Cache). If hit rate drops < 10% for top 5 routes, try warming cache for hot endpoints.
- Temporary mitigation: route traffic to lower-capacity model variant: update route -> fallbackModel: gpt-13b-quant-lite (can be done via Console or API).
- Note: inform infra oncall before changing route-wide model if >5% traffic is affected.

B) Autoscaler oscillation (pods scale up/down every few minutes):
- Look at HPA metrics in last 30m. If target utilization set too low, bump to 65% for the night.
- Quick patch (if documented in infra PR): adjust HPA threshold in `infra/overrides/night-thresholds.yaml` and apply `kubectl apply -f ...` (see linked PR).

C) Model mount flapping (s3/remote storage errors):
- Symptoms: logs include 'Failed to open model weights' or transient 5xx when loading.
- Quick workaround: restart the specific modelserver pod to retry mount after s3 transient error.
- If recurring, escalate to storage team with recent pod logs + failure timestamps (attach pod log snippet).

Escalation quick map (who to ping in order):
1) Oncall infra (Ravi) - kubernetes, autoscaling, node issues.
2) Serving runtime lead (Elena) - modelserver, caching, runtime kernels.
3) Storage (SRE-storage) - external mounts, s3 errors.
4) Prod-eng manager (on-call rota) if customer impact > 1% of traffic for >30m.

Notes on communication:
- Add short status updates to the incident thread every 20 minutes once incident declared. Keep one action per update.
- If applying config changes, include rollback steps in the thread (timestamped).

Temporary workaround snippets I used (log/forensics included):
- 2026-02-25 03:12 UTC: p95 latency spike traced to two modelservers stuck in DRAINING state. Quick fix: restarted inference-router and pooled traffic to replicas. Logs indicated a kernel selection failure for quantized kernels. Posted link to PR #2123 which contains a mitigation.
- 2026-01-07 01:05 UTC: s3 timeout caused model mount failures for 'redwood-vect-13b'. Workaround: restart pod + set MODEL_DOWNLOAD_RETRIES=5 as env override for next rollout. TODO: add to config template if repeats.

Tips to next person (notes to self):
- If you see repeated OOM for a single pod but node has free GPU memory, check for stuck KV cache processes (they don't free memory until restart). Restarting modelserver is usually enough.
- Be conservative with route->fallback changes. Small experiments are fine but monitor cost and tail latency.
- If in doubt, take a short pause and call infra lead — obnoxious rollbacks are worse than slow recovery.

Open questions / things to follow up:
- Should we add a night-specific autoscaler profile? (INF-4872) — action: coordinate with Ravi.
- Investigate whether MODEL_DOWNLOAD_RETRIES change caused slower cold-starts during one test deploy. Follow-up with experiments in staging.

TODO (for post-shift):
- Paste the kernel-selection log from 2026-02-25 into Confluence (link to INF-4872).
- Add a 'warmup' job that preloads top-10 models at 01:30 UTC for 15 minutes.
- Draft a short blameless postmortem if the mount flapping repeats.

Random scratch (safe to delete):
- I keep forgetting the exact k8s label for the inference-router: it's `app=inference-router` not `name=router` — burned me once.
- If you need to temporarily drain a node: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` but only after confirming replicas can move.

End-of-shift handoff checklist (what I always try to leave behind):
- Incident thread updated? (Y/N)
- Any restart or config changes documented in the thread + rollback? (Y/N)
- TODOs added to #oncall-night or assigned in Jira (if >30m follow-up)? (Y/N)
- Brief note to next oncall in Slack: @next-oncall short summary + link to thread.

If anything is unclear ping me (Maya) or check the infra PR linked above. If this ever actually gets promoted, move the reliable bits into `confluence -> Runbooks -> Night Watch`.

-- end of scratchpad (delete before finalizing)
